important: Exemption from a permit does not exempt the work from applicable building, rehabilitation, zoning, development, utility, or other code requirements.
building: One-story detached accessory tool/storage sheds, playhouses, garages, carports, and similar structures with projected roof area no more than 200 square feet.
Oil derricks.
Movable cases, counters, and partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches.
Retaining walls no taller than 4 feet measured from low-side grade, unless they support a surcharge, impound flammable liquids, or adjoin public right-of-way.
Fences, subject to separate zoning and Chapter 27 requirements.
Grade-supported water tanks no larger than 5,000 gallons with height-to-width/diameter ratio no greater than 2:1.
Platforms and decks no more than 30 inches above grade at any point and not above a basement or lower story.
Temporary motion-picture, television, and theater sets/scenery.
Wall-supported window awnings at Group R-3 and U occupancies projecting no more than 54 inches.
Prefabricated pools accessory to Group R-3 that are under 24 inches deep, entirely above adjacent grade, and no larger than 5,000 gallons.

Qualifying reroofing of one- and two-family homes with light roof covering, and other code-compliant reroofing limited to coverings; sheathing/deck replacement and structural alterations are not exempt.
Public-utility generation, communication, transmission, and distribution facilities; utility administrative offices are not exempt.
Replacement exterior wall coverings on detached one- and two-family dwellings.
Replacement doors/windows in existing openings where fire-resistance, smoke-control, and opening-protection rules do not apply.
Repairing holes in plaster or gypsum-board walls.
Installing or replacing wall- or floor-mounted cabinets.
Painting, papering, carpeting/floor coverings, and similar finish work.
Installing or replacing exterior gutters and downspouts.
Tuck-pointing brick or stone masonry.
Replacing less than 32 square feet of soffit or wall/roof sheathing on a one- or two-family dwelling.
Replacing interior or exterior trim.
Boarding vacant buildings.
Walks, patios, and driveways placed on existing grade.
Nursery/agricultural shade-cloth structures, excluding service systems.
Swings and other playground equipment at one- and two-family dwellings.
Building-official-approved isolated grading with no danger to public/private property.

Excavation for basements/footings tied to a valid permit; cemetery graves; otherwise-authorized refuse sites; utility wells/trenches; lawful mining/quarry operations that preserve adjacent lateral support; and exploratory excavation supervised by soils engineers/geologists.
Excavation less than 2 feet deep, or not creating a cut slope over 5 feet high or steeper than 1.5 horizontal to 1 vertical.
Fill on terrain flatter than 5:1 that does not block drainage and is either under 1 foot deep, or under 3 feet/50 cubic yards per parcel and does not support structures.
Ordinary maintenance/resurfacing of an existing code-compliant parking surface.
mechanical: Replacing appliance parts/assemblies without changing original approval and while complying with the code.
Refrigeration equipment that is part of already-permitted equipment.
Replacing grilles and diffusers on existing ductwork.
Self-contained refrigeration systems with no more than 10 pounds of refrigerant or motors no larger than 1 horsepower.
Qualifying franchised/authorized public-utility facilities; administrative offices are not exempt.
plumbing: Repairs limited to faucet or valve working parts.
Repair/replacement of defective fixtures or valves without altering or extending piping.
Replacing or repairing lavatory and sink traps.
Qualifying franchised/authorized public-utility facilities; administrative offices are not exempt.
elevator: ANSI A92 mobile scaffolds, towers, and platforms.
ASME B20.1 conveyors and related equipment.
ASME B30 cranes, derricks, hoists, hooks, jacks, and slings.
Portable equipment other than portable escalators.
Machine-tool/printing-press material feeding or positioning equipment.
Skip or furnace hoists; wharf ramps; amusement devices; stage/orchestra lifts; lift bridges; railroad-car lifts/dumpers; mechanized parking equipment.
Elevator-installation line jacks, false cars, shafters, moving platforms, and similar installation equipment.
Mine elevators outside/away from buildings and qualifying ASME 90.1 man-lifts.
Ship/offshore-platform loading elevators and shipboard elevators.
Qualifying franchised/authorized public-utility facilities; administrative offices are not exempt.
electrical: Minor repairs such as lamp replacement and connecting approved portable equipment to approved permanent receptacles.
Qualifying franchised/authorized public-utility facilities; administrative offices are not exempt.
Power/public-service-company equipment used for its own generation, transmission, distribution, or metering.
Temporary systems used only to test or service electrical equipment/apparatus.
Replacing snap switches, receptacles, and fixtures other than ceiling fans when no circuit alteration or extension is needed.
sign: Changing advertising copy/messages on painted or printed signs; electric signs generally do not qualify except replaceable-copy theater marquees and similar signs.
Painting, repainting, or cleaning an advertising structure, or changing its copy/message without structural change.
Signs inside buildings or on the inside/outside of buses, taxicabs, and other vehicles.
Lettering painted directly on building walls, windows, or doors advertising the owner/occupant or products made, sold, or stored there.
Municipal/traffic, danger, railroad-crossing, legal/trespass, and qualifying public-service safety signs.
One on-premises real-estate sale/rental/lease sign per street frontage, no larger than 32 square feet gross area.
Noncombustible wall tablets limited to owner/building name or use, erection date, or commemorative matter.
Construction-project signs naming the architect, engineer, contractors, enterprise, or building purpose.
Public-service-company signs identifying danger, ownership, offices, or service locations when flat against a wall/structure.
Signs under 10 square feet in residential zoning districts.
